claim: Initial in vivo studies with YKL-05-099 showed increased bone formation and reduced bone resorption.

claim: Tamoxifen treatment (1 mg IP every other day, three injections total) in 6-week-old mice led to robust Sik2 and Sik3, but not Sik1, deletion in cortical bone.

claim: BUN and fasting glucose levels were unaffected by global SIK2/3 ablation in mice treated with tamoxifen at 6 weeks of age.

claim: YKL-05-099-associated toxicities of hyperglycemia and increased BUN are likely due to either SIK1 inhibition or off-target effects of this pharmacologic agent.

claim: Similar changes were observed 4 weeks after Sik2/3 gene deletion in 12-week-old mice including increased trabecular bone, increased cortical porosity, increased levels of bone turnover markers, and increased marrow stromal cells with abnormal growth plate appearance.

claim: The ubiquitin-CreERt2 transgene is active in bone marrow myeloid lineage cells.

claim: 4-OHT treatment led to robust deletion of Sik2 and Sik3 but not Sik1 in bone marrow macrophages.

claim: Upon ex vivo 4-OHT treatment, TKO bone marrow macrophages showed >80% SIK gene deletion.

claim: No significant differences were noted in osteoclast differentiation and function between control and SIK1/2/3 TKO cells.

Similar to SIK2/3 DKO osteoclasts, no significant differences were noted in osteoclast differentiation and function between control and SIK1/2/3 TKO cells (Figure 6B–F).

claim: Increased bone resorption in SIK2/3 DKO mice is likely due to increased RANKL expression from osteoblast lineage cells similar to effects observed with PTH.
source: Taken together, these data argue against an important cell-intrinsic role for SIKs in osteoclasts. Moreover, these results suggest that increased bone resorption in SIK2/3 DKO mice is due to non-cell autonomous actions of SIK gene deletion, likely due to increased RANKL expression from osteoblast lineage cells similar to effects observed with PTH (Wein et al., 2016; Nishimori et al., 2019; Ricarte et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citations to Wein et al., 2016; Nishimori et al., 2019; Ricarte et al., 2018

claim: Of the 58 reporter elements tested by TF-seq, only CRE activity was significantly regulated by YKL-05-099 treatment.

evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1

claim: When phosphorylated by SIKs, CRTC proteins are retained in the cytoplasm.
source: These findings are consistent with a known action of SIKs to regulate the activity of CRTC family CREB coactivators. When phosphorylated by SIKs, CRTC proteins are retained in the cytoplasm. Upon dephosphorylation (in this case in response to SIK inhibitor treatment), CRTC proteins translocate into the nucleus where they potentiate CREB-mediated gene expression (Sakamoto et al., 2018; Wein et al., 2018; Altarejos and Montminy, 2011).
evidence: Supported by citations to Sakamoto et al., 2018; Wein et al., 2018; Altarejos and Montminy, 2011
